conversation.text:
Description: In the Study, an unidentified stranger is found dead. It is initially judged to be a non-violent death, triggering an emergency response involving calling the police and internal confidentiality.
Key Information:
  - The death incident takes place in the Study (Study).
  - An unknown male stranger, previously unmentioned or introduced by anyone, is found on site and confirmed dead.
  - Damian Maseko confirms the deceased is not breathing; the body is still warm, indicating the time of death was not long ago.
  - No obvious external injuries are found; Damian Maseko preliminarily infers the cause of death as a heart attack.
  - Martha Galley explicitly states she does not know the deceased and denies that anyone reported this person entering the villa to her.
  - John Hobbes becomes dizzy on site and apologizes for breaking the bottle.
  - The sound of a bottle dropping and shattering is recorded; combined with earlier node information, it can be confirmed as the wine bottle carried by the visitor.
  - The deceased has very few personal belongings; only a player piano paper roll is found.
  - The name “Amelia West (Amelia West)” appears on the paper roll, and no one present has heard of the name.
  - Martha Galley decides to call the police and instructs Damian Maseko to fetch Harry Thornton (Thornton).
  - Martha Galley proposes keeping the death incident confidential until the police arrive.
  - Martha Galley then takes John Hobbes to the Dining room (Dining room) to rest, and the three leave the Study together.
Characters:
  [Martha Galley (Martha Galley)] Person No. 5, one of the villa’s hostesses.
    · Immediately asks about the deceased’s condition and confirms she does not know him.
    · Is shocked and angry that a stranger entered the villa without being reported.
    · Accepts Damian Maseko’s preliminary judgment about the cause of death.
    · Decides to call the police to handle the death incident.
    · Proposes keeping the incident confidential until the police arrive.
    · Arranges for John Hobbes to leave the Study and rest in the Dining room.
  [John Hobbes (John Hobbes)] Person No. 1, the visitor.
    · Witnesses the death incident in the Study.
    · Experiences dizziness and is in poor condition.
    · Apologizes to Martha Galley for breaking the wine bottle.
    · Denies having anything to do with the deceased or the death incident.
    · Leaves the Study and goes to rest in the Dining room under Martha Galley’s arrangement.
  [Damian Maseko (Damian)] Person No. 8, one of the villa residents.
    · Confirms the deceased is not breathing and judges that he is dead.
    · Notes that the body is still warm and the time of death was not long ago.
    · Examines the body and finds no obvious external injuries.
    · Based on the deceased’s age and condition, preliminarily infers the cause of death as a heart attack.
    · Finds and reports the player piano paper roll carried by the deceased.
    · Follows Martha Galley’s instruction to go fetch Harry Thornton (Thornton).
  [Amelia West (Amelia West)] A name appearing among the deceased’s personal effects.
    · The name appears on the player piano paper roll.
    · No one present has heard of the name.
  [Harry Thornton (Thornton)] A person Martha Galley specifically orders to be called over.
    · Is considered necessary to be involved in handling the current death incident.
